skill.name: quality-reviewer
skill.description: Deep code review workflow that checks project standards, current documentation, library versions, and security advisories.
skill.summary: Review code quality against project context and current ecosystem guidance.
skill.author: ArcadeAI

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution alerts are false positives from markdown fences, inline code, and a hardcoded read-only ls example. No malware, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found, but the skill grants overbroad tool access through a wildcard permission.

remediation.suggestion: Replace allowed-tools: '*' with the minimum tools needed, such as Read, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch, and constrained read-only Bash.
Keep shell examples hardcoded and read-only. Avoid examples that mutate files, install packages, or upload project data.

static_findings.snippet: - Did the library's recommendations change recently?

finding_verdicts.reason: The fenced bash block contains a single hardcoded ls command for local project standards files. It is read-only and does not use dynamic input or Ruby backtick execution.
This line is the closing markdown fence for the prior example. It is not executable code and has no command execution behavior.
The backticks mark the filename CLAUDE.md as inline markdown text. There is no shell execution, interpolation, or external command invocation.
This range covers prose review guidance and inline markdown terms, not executable script content. I found no dynamic command construction or unsafe command request in this range.
The line opens a text output example block. It does not execute a command or instruct the agent to run shell code.
This line closes a markdown text example. It is formatting only and contains no executable instruction.
The line opens a markdown output format example. It is documentation for report formatting, not command execution.
The line asks whether library recommendations changed recently as part of documentation review. It is not host reconnaissance or collection of system information.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Tool Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares allowed-tools: '*' for a workflow that includes filesystem inspection and web research. Broad permissions increase impact if instructions are misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wildcard permission is explicit in the skill metadata, and the review workflow only needs a smaller set of read and research tools.

content.value_statement: Developers need reviews that catch bugs, outdated libraries, and documentation drift before changes ship. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a current, standards-aware code review.
actual_capabilities: Reviews recent code changes for correctness, edge cases, and error handling.
Checks changes against CLAUDE.md, SAFEWORD.md, and architecture guidance when present.
Researches current library versions, security advisories, and official documentation.
Flags outdated dependencies, deprecated APIs, and changed best practices.
Produces concise verdicts with critical issues and suggested improvements.
limitations: Requires internet access for current version and documentation checks.
Does not replace automated tests, static analysis, or formal security review.
Needs clear change context to identify the relevant files.
Can miss private project rules if they are not documented.

use_cases.title: Pre-Merge Review
use_cases.description: Review recent changes for correctness, edge cases, project standards, and release blockers before merging.

use_cases.title: Dependency Audit
use_cases.description: Check selected libraries against current versions, security advisories, and official migration guidance.

use_cases.title: Architecture Review
use_cases.description: Compare an implementation with documented architecture principles and suggest focused improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Change Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my recent changes for correctness, edge cases, and blocking issues. Use project standards if available.

prompt_templates.title: Dependency Version Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with current version research
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this implementation and verify the main libraries against current stable versions and security advisories.

prompt_templates.title: Documentation Compatibility Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this code with the latest official docs for the frameworks it uses. Flag deprecated APIs and newer recommended patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release review across quality dimensions
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full quality review before release. Check correctness, bloat, maintainability, standards, versions, docs, and security-sensitive dependencies.

output_examples.input: Review a recent UI change before merge.
output: Correctness is sound for the main flow.
One edge case needs a loading-state check.
No dependency concerns were found after documentation review.

output_examples.input: Check whether a framework upgrade is safe.
output: The installed major version is behind the current stable release.
The official migration guide lists one breaking change in routing.
Upgrade after adding coverage for the affected route behavior.

output_examples.input: Audit code against project architecture rules.
output: The implementation follows the documented ownership boundary.
One helper duplicates existing shared logic.
Request changes for the duplication before approval.

best_practices: Provide the diff, affected files, and the goal of the change.
Ask for official documentation checks when library behavior matters.
Separate blocking issues from optional cleanup in the final verdict.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as the only test or security gate.
Do not ask for broad web research when the change is local and simple.
Do not ignore project standards files when they exist.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is designed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require web access?
faq.answer: Web access is needed for current version, vulnerability, and documentation checks.

faq.question: Can it replace automated tests?
faq.answer: No. It complements tests by adding human-style review and current ecosystem checks.

faq.question: What inputs improve the review?
faq.answer: Provide the changed files, intended behavior, dependencies involved, and any project standards documents.

faq.question: Will it modify code?
faq.answer: No. It is a review workflow unless the user separately asks for edits.

faq.question: Can it find security issues?
faq.answer: It can flag risky patterns and vulnerable dependencies, but it is not a formal penetration test.
